correctness.rationale: Fresh exhaustive code independently enumerates all 46,656 profiles, implements student-proposing DA and school-choice TTC from their definitions, and separately tests DA Pareto efficiency against all six perfect matchings. It reproduces 42,336 equal, 1,080 TTC-dominant, 3,240 incomparable and zero DA-dominant profiles, together with the 1,296 inefficient DA count and 216 inefficient-but-incomparable profiles. An independent canonical action of all 36 role-preserving relabelings yields exactly 120 divergent orbits, each of size 36, refined as 30 TTC-dominant/inefficient, 84 efficient-incomparable and 6 inefficient-incomparable.

evidence: These papers treat arbitrary finite priority-based allocation problems and mechanism properties.
Their structural conclusions do not enumerate the first nontrivial finite domain.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader mechanism theorems do not imply the exact profile frequencies or orbit refinement.

originality.rationale: The mechanism-design literature already proves that DA can be inefficient, TTC is Pareto efficient, and the two mechanisms need not be Pareto comparable even when DA is inefficient. Those qualitative facts are treated as prior. The audited contribution is the complete first-divergence finite census and role-preserving symmetry quotient. No inspected primary source or Resultary finding gives the counts 42,336/1,080/3,240, the 216-profile exceptional stratum, or the 120-class quotient.

value.rationale: The 3x3 market is the first size at which these two canonical school-choice mechanisms diverge. A complete labeled and symmetry-reduced census quantifies exactly how the known qualitative efficiency/non-dominance phenomena first arise, making it a natural finite boundary benchmark rather than an arbitrary enumeration.
residual_risks: An unindexed computational appendix, thesis or teaching dataset could contain the same small-market census.

final_claim: For strict unit-capacity school choice through size three, DA and TTC agree for n≤2; at n=3, among all 46,656 labeled preference-priority profiles they agree on 42,336, TTC Pareto-dominates DA on 1,080, and are incomparable on 3,240, with exactly 1,296 inefficient DA profiles and the stated 120-class S3×S3 quotient.
limitations: Strict complete preferences/priorities, unit capacities and n≤3 only.
Known qualitative DA/TTC efficiency and non-dominance phenomena are prior art; novelty is the exact first-size census and quotient.
